Angle C is the right angle, so C=90^\circ.

The two acute angles are complementary, so B=90^\circ-A=90^\circ-55.3^\circ=34.7^\circ.

With the side opposite A given, use the sine ratio: \sin A=\frac{a}{c}, so c=\frac{a}{\sin A}=\frac{3.5}{\sin 55.3^\circ}\approx 4.26\text{ ft}.

The tangent ratio gives the other leg: \tan A=\frac{a}{b}, so b=\frac{a}{\tan A}=\frac{3.5}{\tan 55.3^\circ}\approx 2.42\text{ ft}.

Collecting the results, angles first and then sides: A = 55.3^\circ, B = 34.7^\circ, C = 90^\circ; a = 3.5\text{ ft}, b \approx 2.42\text{ ft}, c \approx 4.26\text{ ft}.
